\chapter{Stay in May}
\label{ch:quedarse-mayo}
\hlchaptermodality{416}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can understand the month and length of a simple hotel stay.}

Retrieve stay and May in a short hotel booking exchange.

\section[quedarse]{quedarse — come to rest and stay}

\label{lesson:ES-C416-quedarse}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{una habitación}, a room. A traveller who keeps that room for several nights is going to \textbf{quedarse}, to stay.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Spanish \textbf{quedar} reaches back to Latin \textbf{quietāre}, to make quiet or bring to rest. The \textbf{se} turns the action toward the person: \textbf{quedarse} is to remain or stay. Think of a traveller coming to rest in one place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: say who stays}]
The pronoun changes with the person: \textbf{me quedo} means “I stay,” while the infinitive follows another verb in \textbf{quiero quedarme}, “I want to stay.” A duration can follow directly: \textbf{quedarse tres noches}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{quedarse}
  \item \emph{me quedo tres noches}
  \item \emph{quiero quedarme tres noches}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To stay? (\emph{Quedarse}.) I am staying three nights? (\emph{Me quedo tres noches}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/quedar}{DLE: quedar}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mayo]{mayo — Maia's month}

\label{lesson:ES-C416-mayo}



\begin{quote}
Recall the months and \textbf{quedarse}, to stay. The hotel dates in this chapter fall in \textbf{mayo}, May.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Spanish \textbf{mayo} continues Latin \textbf{Maius}, the Roman month associated with \textbf{Maia}. English \textbf{May} preserves the same name. Keep it separate from \textbf{mayor}, “bigger” or “older”: their similar spelling does not make them the same word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: dates use de}]
Spanish links a day to its month with \textbf{de}: \textbf{el quince de mayo}, the fifteenth of May. A range uses \textbf{del ... al ...}: \textbf{del quince al dieciocho de mayo}. The month name stays lowercase.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{mayo}
  \item \emph{el quince de mayo}
  \item \emph{quedarse tres noches en mayo}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
May? (\emph{Mayo}.) The fifteenth of May? (\emph{El quince de mayo}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/mayo}{DLE: mayo}.
\end{tcolorbox}
